Article Title: 'They have the right to protest, argue': Ex-BJP leader Annamalai questions govt's handling of CJP protests
Article Text:
‘I disagree with CJP’s protest strategies’

NEW DELHI: Former Tamil Nadu BJP chief K Annamalai has questioned the Centre over its handling of protests by the CJP group in Delhi, raising concerns over restrictions at Jantar Mantar, preventive detention and bail proceedings involving its office-bearers.In a series of posts, former BJP leader K Annamalai invoked then-Gujarat CM Narendra Modi’s 2011 remarks condemning the police crackdown on an anti-corruption protest at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan, questioning whether the principles Modi defended then applied to protesters today.“In 2011, the then Gujarat chief minister, Narendra Modi, said that if his hands had not been tied, he would have gone to Delhi and revolted against the central government,” Annamalai wrote.“In my view, what the honourable Prime Minister Narendra Modi said then was absolutely right. There was nothing wrong with it,” he added.Annamalai, who said he left the BJP on June 5, 2026, questioned how Jantar Mantar was removed as a designated protest site after CJP sought permission to hold a demonstration.He also raised concerns over an assistant commissioner of police (ACP) functioning as a special executive magistrate with the authority to decide whether a person should remain in preventive detention.“In the CJP case, Delhi Police itself is the complainant, while an ACP belonging to the same Delhi Police force has the authority to decide whether the accused should remain in preventive detention,” he said.He also questioned why eight bail sureties had been rejected and why a magistrate had cross-examined a person offering bail surety. Annamalai further asked whether action had been taken over the alleged use of pellet guns and other standard operating procedure violations during protests against the NEET examination.Comparing the situation with protests during previous Congress and Aam Aadmi Party governments in Delhi, he asked how BJP workers who allegedly jumped barricades or disobeyed police orders had been treated.“Was it anything like what is happening now? Certainly not!” he said.Annamalai said he disagreed with CJP’s approach but defended its right to protest.“As I said yesterday, I do not agree with CJP’s protest strategies, and I believe many of its approaches are misguided,” he said.“But if you ask me whether they have the right to protest, argue and fight for an issue they consider important, my answer is an unequivocal yes!” he added.He also criticised the tendency to portray protests against the Union government as anti-national or foreign-funded.“It is genuinely exhausting and frustrating to see every protest against the central government and every statement it issues being portrayed as an anti-national act funded by foreign powers,” he said.Annamalai further questioned whether the BJP was inadvertently giving CJP publicity by targeting it, referring to a Dussehra event led by BJP MLA Ashok Goyal.“Is the BJP genuinely opposed to CJP, or is it giving the organisation free publicity?” he asked.The remarks come days after CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were arrested over an alleged attempt to trespass at Jantar Mantar, which had been de-notified as a designated protest site. They were sent to Tihar Jail and later released after signing a bond.
Article Summary: Former Tamil Nadu BJP chief K Annamalai has questioned the Centre over its handling of protests by the CJP group in Delhi. He has raised concerns over restrictions at Jantar Mantar, preventive detention and bail proceedings involving its office-bearers. He also questioned whether the BJP was inadvertently giving CJP publicity by targeting it.

Article Title: 'You want to protect infiltrators' votes': Amit Shah's sharp attack on Rahul Gandhi over 'vote theft' claims
Article Text:
Amit Shah takes on Rahul over polls, Kejriwal over Yamuna and Punjab drugs

‘Yamuna will be cleaned by May 2029’

Shah targets AAP over Punjab drug menace

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Thursday hit out at leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi over his allegations of “vote chori” and "collusion" between the Election Commission and the BJP , accusing the Congress of using the issue to explain its electoral defeats.Addressing an event in Delhi on his birthday where he launched projects worth Rs 8,941 crore for cleaning the Yamuna, Shah also targeted the Arvind Kejriwal-led Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) over its governance in Delhi and Punjab.“The BJP keeps winning elections, and the opposition is troubled by it. That is why they have come up with the excuse of ‘vote chori’, or vote theft,” Shah said.“Rahul ji, you keep talking about vote theft because you want to protect the votes of infiltrators,” he added.Union home minister argued that the BJP had been winning elections in several states even before Narendra Modi became prime minister, while the Congress had remained out of power in many states for decades.“Congress, its allies accuse BJP of vote theft but are out of power in many states for decades,” he said.Referring to the Congress's electoral record, Shah cited its prolonged absence from power in several states and questioned whether its electoral setbacks had begun only after Modi became prime minister.“When I say the BJP will remain in power for 30 years, they accuse us of stealing votes. They ask how Amit Shah knows the election results in advance. Amit Shah was born here, lives here and will die here. I do not have to travel abroad every six months. I live among the people of this country,” he said.Attacking Lok Sabha LoP he said, "When court rulings favour you, you call them fair, but when they go against you, you question them. These double standards will not work, Rahul ji."Shah also targeted Rahul over opposition protests in Delhi, saying, “You cannot overturn the people's mandate through political manoeuvres and mob pressure. Winning elections is not about staging protests and sit-ins.”Shah also accused previous governments in Delhi of failing to prevent untreated sewage from entering the Yamuna and said the BJP government was committed to cleaning the river.“Congress, AAP govts allowed discharge of sewer water in Yamuna; we will clean it by May 2029,” Shah said.The projects launched at the event are aimed at improving sewage treatment and wastewater management, expanding sewer connections and reducing pollution in the river.Turning to poll-bound Punjab, where the AAP government is led by chief minister Bhagwant Mann, Shah attacked the ruling party over the drug menace and expressed confidence that the NDA would come to power in the state.“Drug menace prevalent in Punjab; people of state want NDA government,” he said.“AAP is going to be routed in Punjab elections , we will end drug trafficking in state,” Shah added.
Article Summary: Union home minister Amit Shah hit out at leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi. He accused the Congress of using the issue to explain its electoral defeats. Shah also targeted the Arvind Kejriwal-led Aam Aadmi Party over its governance in Delhi and Punjab.

Article Title: 'This evil man will be punished': Union minister Rijiju warns Delhi influencer over 'racial' abuse of Tripura youth
Article Text:
From Rijiju to Tripura opposition, outrage over alleged racial abuse of tribal youth

NEW DELHI: Union minister Kiren Rijiju late Wednesday strongly condemned "racial" harassment of a tribal youth from Tripura's Gomati district by a Delhi-based social media influencer Amir Shokeen.Rijiju took to X and shared a video of the incident, acknowledging the delay in filing an official complaint but warning that the accused would face action."This evil man will be punished. There was delay in lodging the official complaint but Delhi Police and Tripura Police will teach him a hard lesson. People who tolerate such wicked behavior in the society are also responsible for the spread of hatred," the Union parliamentary affairs minister said.In the video circulating online, Shokeen can allegedly be heard making racial remarks against the youth. The clip, which surfaced on Tuesday evening, purportedly shows him asking the young man whether he was the "president" of a neighbouring country. He allegedly mocked Tripura when the youth responded that he was Indian.Political parties in Tripura closed ranks on Wednesday over the incident and demanded legal action against Shokeen.Tripura chief minister Manik Saha directed the state director general of police to coordinate with Delhi Police and ensure a proper investigation into the incident.CPM state secretary and leader of the opposition Jitendra Chaudhury demanded an apology from Shokeen. "Establish a precedent that is both resounding and unmistakable, ensuring no one ever dares insult Tripura and the Tiprasa community again," he said.Congress MLA Sudip Roy Barman called for a joint protest in Delhi, saying, "This type of attitude is intolerable."Meanwhile, Shokeen posted a video on Facebook claiming that the incident was scripted. He said the person he allegedly abused was an acquaintance who worked at a friend's cafe in Ahmedabad."I did not intend to insult the people of Tripura, and I apologise if my words hurt anyone," he said.
Article Summary: Kiren Rijiju condemns "racial" harassment of a tribal youth from Tripura's Gomati district by a Delhi-based social media influencer. The clip purportedly shows him asking the young man whether he was the "president" of a neighbouring country. He allegedly mocked Tripura when the youth responded that he was Indian.

Article Title: CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka summoned by Delhi Police day after release

CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka summoned

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party ( CJP ) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka have been summoned by the Delhi Police Crime Branch to its Rajouri Garden office on Thursday, a day after they were released from judicial custody.The two leaders were released after a Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) court accepted their personal and surety bonds and recorded their written undertakings to maintain peace and abide by the law.SEM Ritu Raj directed Das and Ranka to furnish personal and surety bonds of Rs 50,000 each until the conclusion of the enquiry. They were also asked to appear on every hearing date and comply with the conditions specified in their bonds and undertakings.In their written undertakings, the leaders promised not to breach peace or disturb public tranquillity. They also undertook not to call for protests at Jantar Mantar until the site is denotified in accordance with the law, and said any future protests would be held within the constitutional framework.Delhi Police had earlier sought a further three-day extension of their judicial custody, citing concerns over a possible breach of peace and law and order.Police also pointed to alleged differences between statements made by the leaders before the court and their subsequent remarks to the media.The two leaders were detained in connection with an October 13 protest at Jantar Mantar, which had been denotified as a designated protest site. Police alleged that they entered the area through private premises and violated conditions relating to maintaining peace.The court directed the investigating officer to submit a report verifying the sureties at the next hearing. The matter is listed for further proceedings on October 23 at 3 pm, with Das, Ranka and their sureties directed to remain present.

Article Title: Tiger shooters got weapons via ‘dead drop’; couriers delivered guns a day earlier
Article Text:
The accused in the Tiger firing case were sent to police custody till Oct 31.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The shooters involved in the attack on actor Tiger Shroff received their weapons through a “dead drop” arrangement on Oct 17, just a day before the incident. Couriers Babita and Radha — who have since been arrested — were provided the weapons at New Delhi Railway Station by the main supplier, identified as Kunal.Kunal, who has also been arrested, has emerged as a key character who had been in touch with gangsters Anil Pandit and Randeep Malik for over two months. He had also figured as the source of the weapon used for the murder of a forex-hawala trader in Sonipat last year, sources said.In this case, he was relaying the instructions from Pandit to the two women after dropping them at the station on Oct 15. The women reached Mumbai on Oct 17, got off at Dadar and checked into a hotel. Around 11am, one of the shooters collected the bag with the weapons at an isolated spot near the hotel, an official added.The dead drop method — borrowed from spycraft — has increasingly surfaced in investigations involving terror modules, drug cartels and organised crime groups of late. Agencies have unearthed non-contact logistics where handlers use encrypted messaging to direct operatives to pre-arranged locations to collect weapons, funds and synthetic drugs.Some cases in point include IS-linked terror modules, cross-border drone-dropped payloads along the Punjab and J&K frontiers, interstate gang firearm procurements and synthetic drug delivery networks.Investigators reconstruct digital footprints, chat logs and GPS coordinates alongside CCTV footage analysis to establish the timeline. By using technical surveillance, cell tower dumps and financial intelligence tied to encrypted communications, agencies are able to intercept these isolated drop routines to cut off unverified supplier-courier links, sources said.
Article Summary: The shooters involved in the attack on actor Tiger Shroff received their weapons through a ‘dead drop’ arrangement on Oct 17, just a day before the incident. Couriers Babita and Radha were provided the weapons at New Delhi Railway Station by the main supplier.

Article Title: Confidence in poll process key for democracy, halt list of candidates: SC to AP SEC
Article Text:
SC said the right to participate in elections by filing nominations is a facet of the free poll process.

YSRCP importing criminals from Punjab: AP govt in SC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Wednesday said instilling confidence in the election process was vital for democracy and the rule of law as it directed Andhra Pradesh State Election Commission (SEC) not to declare the final candidate list for 19 of the 100 local bodies where opposition YSRCP has alleged that its candidates were prevented from filing nominations. However, the court refused to tinker with the Oct 28 polling date.An autumn-break bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and VMohana asked SEC to decide by Thursday if it should, after considering representations from candidates alleging use of force to prevent them from filing nominations, give additional time for filing of nominations or postpone polls. Accepting the suggestion of senior advocate Maninder Singh, who appeared for YSRCP, SC asked DGP to give adequate security at nomination filing centres and to candidates.Senior advocate Maninder Singh, who appeared for YSRCP, said in 19 of the 100 urban local bodies — 13 municipal corporations and 87 municipalities/nagar panchayats — more than 63% of YSRCP candidates were prevented from filing nominations or their nomination papers were torn. Senior advocate Sidharth Luthra, for AP govt, said YSRCP was importing criminal elements from as far as Punjab and fomenting violence only to cry wolf later.SEC, through senior advocate K Parameswar, denied YSRCP’s claims.The SC bench said, “Free and fair elections are a basic structure of the Constitution. Right to participate in such elections by filing nomination papers is a facet of the free and fair election process. It is the constitutional mandate to vest the SEC with the duty of conducting and supervising such elections which would necessarily include all steps to ensure free and transparent filing of nomination papers by contesting candidates. The power of constitutional courts in exercise of judicial review, though deferential to the conduct of elections by the EC, cannot be said to be only nugatory.”SC said it was the duty of SEC to direct the state law-enforcing machinery to provide adequate security and maintain law and order to provide candidates a secure environment to file their nomination papers in a peaceful manner.Referring to Singh’s allegations that the state police were, at times, indifferent or selective in registering complaints of YSRCP candidates, Parameswar said SEC had issued directions to police and Luthra said police had taken adequate measures to control law and order issues.Referring to the allegations of the principal opposition party, backed by prima facie material of violence unleashed to prevent filing of nominations, SC said, “We are conscious of judicial deference to the powers of control and superintendence of elections by EC. Such philosophy of deference has grown from a doctrine of necessity that the election process be entrusted in the hands of an independent constitutional authority and the process completed within a specified period and not get mired in the quagmire of judicial interference.“...It also cannot be ignored that the custody of constitutional values lies with constitutional courts and the power of judicial review to ensure fair and impartial elections cannot be wholly muted when the principal opposition political party in a state is before us and has placed on record representations and material expressing serious apprehensions with regard to hindrance in participation in election process through filing of nomination papers. ”
Article Summary: Supreme Court said instilling confidence in the election process was vital for democracy and the rule of law. Opposition YSRCP has alleged that its candidates were prevented from filing nominations. The court refused to tinker with the Oct 28 polling date.

NEW DELHI: A special executive magistrate on Wednesday ordered the release of Cockroach Janata Party leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, seven days after they were taken into custody.The CJP leaders were sent to five days of judicial custody on October 13 following a protest at Jantar Mantar seeking CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the deletion of voters' names.CJP leaders Das and Ranka, along with 12 party members, allegedly trespassed into Jantar Mantar, which is no longer a designated protest venue, and obstructed police personnel on duty.The release order came hours after the two withdrew their petition in the Delhi high court challenging the extension of their custody.The CJP leaders were released after they gave written undertakings not to breach the peace and assured the court that they would not call for any protest at Jantar Mantar as long as it remains denotified as a protest site, Live Law reported.The leaders also assured the court that any protest they organise would be conducted within the four corners of the Constitution.Read more | Watch: 'Inquilab Zindabad', CJP leaders Saurav Das & Ashutosh Ranka come out of Tihar Jail In their undertakings, Ranka and Das expressed faith in the judiciary and its institutions, including the court of the special executive magistrate. Article Title: INDIA bloc huddle: Leaders to meet virtually on CEC row; SIR irregularities on agenda
Article Text:
INDIA bloc leaders to meet today to discuss strategy against CEC Gyanesh Kumar

Opposition steps up campaign against Election Commission

Kharge targets immunity law, EVMs

INDIA bloc challenges SIR, Jantar Mantar decision

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Leaders of the INDIA bloc will meet through video conferencing on Thursday evening to discuss their strategy over the ongoing row involving chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, sources cited by news agency ANI said, with Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge set to chair the meeting.The meeting comes as Opposition parties continue their campaign against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demand accountability from the Election Commission of India (ECI).The opposition has accused the poll panel of facilitating the deletion of eligible voters from electoral rolls and has sought Kumar’s resignation.The Election Commission has maintained that it follows established procedures and defended its role in conducting elections.The INDIA bloc had earlier announced a joint action plan under its “Save Democracy” campaign. The proposed programme included protests, a march towards the Election Commission headquarters and a rally in New Delhi on November 1.On October 6, INDIA bloc MPs led by Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi marched towards Nirvachan Sadan, the Election Commission’s headquarters, seeking a meeting with the poll panel.Delhi Police stopped the march amid heavy barricading and detained several opposition leaders, including Rahul Gandhi and Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra. They were later released.Following the protest, the ECI said Delhi Police had informed it that a delegation of around 240 MPs wanted to meet the Election Commissioners and submit a memorandum at the Parliament House Annexe.The poll panel described the proposed venue and manner of seeking the meeting as “unusual” under its established protocol.Delhi Police said the march had not been granted permission and cited prohibitory orders to explain its action against the protesters.The opposition subsequently approached President Droupadi Murmu. An INDIA bloc delegation, including Rahul Gandhi, Kharge, Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee and Samajwadi Party representatives, submitted a memorandum outlining its demands on October 9.The memorandum sought Kumar’s resignation, suspension of the SIR exercise, restoration of voters allegedly deleted from electoral rolls and a return to paper ballots.The opposition also called for the repeal of the 2023 law granting immunity to the chief election commissioner and other election commissioners for official duties.On Wednesday, Kharge accused the BJP-led government of undermining democratic institutions and shielding election officials from accountability. He said the opposition’s campaign was aimed at protecting the Constitution and democracy rather than securing electoral gains for any particular party.Kharge criticised Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, which grants legal immunity to current and former Election Commissioners for official duties.He argued that the provision protected election officials from accountability and demanded its repeal.“We are asking the BJP to repeal that law. Because you are giving protection to the Election Commissioner and letting him make mistakes. And whatever mistakes have happened today, they happened through Gyanesh Kumar. Why did you give him immunity? It was given so that you can make mistakes through him just by telling him to do so, and forgive him. The Chief Justice doesn’t have immunity. The President of India doesn’t have it. An Election Commissioner does,” Kharge said.He also called for Kumar’s removal, the scrapping of electronic voting machines (EVMs) and a return to paper ballots, while demanding stricter checks on changes to voter lists.“Follow the constitutional system, and remove Gyanesh Kumar, whom you have appointed today. Along with removing him, change the system too. Bring the previous law back, get rid of the EVMs, bring back ballot papers, and the software that sits in one place and controls the whole country. Stop using BLOs to make changes to the voter list,” he said.Kharge also criticised the government’s response to opposition concerns, alleging that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah were using ministers and constitutional officials to avoid directly addressing the issues raised by the opposition.At a meeting on October 13, INDIA bloc leaders reiterated their resolve to continue the campaign and said they would challenge the denotification of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site.Opposition leaders, including Rahul Gandhi and Kharge, have also approached the Supreme Court challenging aspects of the SIR exercise.On October 15, the Supreme Court issued notices to the Election Commission, Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi on petitions challenging aspects of the revision exercise.The court also agreed to examine the denotification of Jantar Mantar and directed Delhi Police to preserve CCTV footage of the protests amid allegations of excessive force.Thursday’s meeting is expected to focus on the opposition’s strategy in the continuing dispute with the Election Commission, including its demands over the SIR exercise and accountability of the poll panel.
Article Summary: Leaders of the INDIA bloc will meet through video conferencing on Thursday evening. Meeting comes as Opposition parties continue their campaign against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Opposition has accused the poll panel of facilitating the deletion of eligible voters from electoral rolls and has sought Kumar’s resignation.

Article Title: SC stays probe against Vijayan & kin for a week to enable him to move high court
Article Text:
SC clarified that its observations did not touch upon the merits of the case against Keralam ex-CM Pinarayi Vijayan and his relatives.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Wednesday stayed for a week Kerala Police’s investigation against ex-CM Pinarayi Vijayan and his relatives in the CMRL-Exalogic payoff case and said a division bench of HC should not have refused them permission to appeal against the single judge’s order directing an FIR and probe.A special bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, hearing appeals filed by Vijayan, his daughter Veena T and son-in-law Mohd Riyas PA, stayed the probe by state police.Referring to Section 175(4) of BNSS, which requires a report from the public servant’s superior officer before ordering an investigation into a complaint against the public servant for acts done in discharge of official duties, the bench said, “The single judge not only directed registration of FIR, which is the mandate in SC ruling in Vijay Madanlal case, but ordered commencement of investigation and submission of final report. ”“Commencement of investigation and taking the same to logical conclusion will require due compliance with other statutory requirements under the special law (as laid down in Charanjit Singh judgement of Supreme Court),” it said.“These facts clearly make out a prima facie case of locus standi for the petitioners to seek leave to appeal against (single judge’s) order. Accordingly, we set aside the impugned order and permit the petitioners to pursue their appeals before the division bench of the HC,” it added.SC clarified that its observations did not touch upon the merits of the case. “The investigation into FIR shall remain stayed for seven days,” it said.On an ECIR registered by ED on the basis of the FIR lodged by Kerala Police, the bench said it was not expressing any opinion on its validity.When Kerala govt undertook not to proceed with the probe till division bench decided the appeals, SC said, “Your client was so eager to investigate. We do not appreciate the state govt functioning like this.”On Sept 7, two years after registering an ECIR, ED shared information with state police regarding the alleged payoff case. State govt set up an SIT for a preliminary inquiry. On Oct 9, a single judge set aside the inquiry and directed filing of an FIR, lodged on Oct 12.Vijayan told SC the alleged payments were made between 2017 and 2020 by CMRL to Exalogic, in which he was never a shareholder, director or employee. He said he had no dealings with CMRL and claimed the allegations were examined and rejected at every level up to SC, which dismissed a petition over the issue in October 2025.
Article Summary: Supreme Court stays for a week Kerala Police’s investigation against ex-CM Pinarayi Vijayan and his relatives in the CMRL-Exalogic payoff case. Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, hearing appeals filed by Vijayan, his daughter and son-in-law, stayed the probe by state police.

Article Title: Who are the terrorists? J&K and Ladakh high court questions ‘vague’ detention order
Article Text:
Representative image

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: J&K and Ladakh HC has summoned the Srinagar deputy commissioner for a personal appearance over a “vague” preventive detention order under Public Safety Act that accused a 28-year-old man of supporting “aforementioned terrorists” without identifying a single one, prompting the court to question whether the officer had independently assessed the case or merely reproduced a police dossier.A single bench of Justice Wasim Nargal said preventive detention, which allows authorities to deprive a person of liberty without a regular criminal trial, demands the “highest degree of constitutional responsibility and procedural diligence”.“The safeguards embodied in Articles 21 and 22 of the Constitution of India are not empty formalities,” the court said, adding that the detaining authority must independently assess the material and satisfy itself that legal conditions for detention are met.The court directed the DC to appear with the detention order, police dossier, material placed before him and records showing his consideration of the case and subjective satisfaction before ordering detention under PSA.HC was hearing a habeas corpus petition filed by Zubair Amin Bangroo of Srinagar, challenging his detention under an order dated Jan 13, 2026. His counsel Nida Nazir said the allegations were vague, no FIR had been registered against him and the detention order appeared to have been passed hurriedly.The order accused Bangroo of developing close links with terrorists, supporting them logistically and morally, and allowing his home and other safe locations to be used as hideouts. However, Nazir said it neither identified the terrorists nor named the network or associates with whom Bangroo was allegedly in contact.HC found that the detention grounds referred to “aforementioned terrorists” without any preceding reference identifying a terrorist. The phrase raised a compelling question about whether the DC had independently formulated the grounds or simply reproduced the police dossier, the court said.“Personal liberty occupies a position of paramount importance in the constitutional scheme. Its deprivation, even for a single day, constitutes an injury which cannot subsequently be undone by the mere restoration of liberty,” the court said.
Article Summary: HC was hearing a habeas corpus petition filed by Zubair Amin Bangroo of Srinagar, challenging his detention under an order dated Jan 13, 2026. His counsel Nida Nazir said the allegations were vague, no FIR had been registered against him and the detention order appeared to have been passed hurriedly.

Article Title: ‘I'm not a travel agent’: Shashi Tharoor when asked about Rahul Gandhi's foreign trip
Article Text:
‘I am not a travel agent’: Shashi Tharoor on Rahul Gandhi's foreign trip

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Wednesday declined to comment on Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi ’s overseas visit, saying, “I am not a travel agent.”“There is no point in asking me that question. Why did I leave Delhi and come here now? Every person has certain responsibilities. So, I cannot comment on that,” Tharoor said when asked about Rahul’s travel plans.Tharoor’s remarks came after the BJP stepped up its criticism of Rahul Gandhi over his alleged foreign trip amid opposition protests in Delhi against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The BJP shared a video on X purportedly showing the Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition aboard a flight to Vietnam, saying, “Too tired of spreading lies. Let me tour Vietnam for a while, who would get to know.”BJP leader Shahnawaz Hussain also took a swipe at Gandhi, suggesting he needed a break after his activities during the protests.“Rahul ji was very tired. He worked very hard. Sometimes he went to a police station, sometimes he sat inside All India Radio, sometimes he lay down on the road to get his pictures clicked, sometimes he pushed and shoved police personnel, and sometimes he knocked a journalist to the ground.He works so hard that he gets exhausted,” Hussain said.Congress leader Sandeep Dikshit, however, defended Rahul’s right to travel abroad, questioning the BJP’s criticism.“Who travels where and when... what is the issue? Do others not travel abroad? Rahul Gandhi is an individual and the leader of the opposition. He has his duties. He interacts with students at Yale University, meets students in London and engages with intellectuals there. He even gives press interviews, something the Prime Minister does not do,” Dikshit said.He also cited Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s foreign visits during Parliament sessions, questioning why they had not drawn similar criticism.“We also have a tradition that the Prime Minister does not travel abroad when the Lok Sabha is in session. But our PM broke that tradition. Why does no question arise at that time?” he asked.Rahul has been leading the opposition’s campaign against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the SIR exercise, demanding his resignation. The Election Commission and the BJP have rejected allegations of irregularities in the revision process, accusing Rahul of “spreading lies”.
Article Summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor declined to comment on Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi’s overseas visit. The BJP stepped up its criticism of Rahul Gandhi over his alleged foreign trip amid opposition protests in Delhi against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The Election Commission and the BJP have rejected allegations of irregularities in the revision process.

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke in another X post on Monday claimed that the local Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) in his hometown had “suddenly gone on leave” and that a new officer had been brought in to take charge.Dipke’s remarks came amid party's earlier claim that he and fellow CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Dass could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other provisions.AISA national president Neha Bora on Monday claimed that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station.In a post on X, Neha said "Rosy and other protesting journalists are detained at Delhi Cantt PS. Team of lawyer comrades are in touch with them.But if any lawyer can be at the PS immediately, pls DM."Rosie is among the three female journalists who filed complaint alleging sexual harassment by police personnel during a protest in the New Delhi area on October 3.The complants have been transferred to the Crime Branch at Kamla Market for further action.Delhi Police also detained several protesters outside Parliament Street Police Station who were demonstrating over an alleged incident of sexual misconduct involving three women journalists during an October 3 protest at Jantar Mantar.The protesters alleged that they had been demonstrating since 6pm on Sunday, demanding registration of an FIR in the case. Police detained them around 7am on Monday following a clash, with protesters alleging they were treated poorly despite only seeking registration of an FIR. Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Derek O’Brien also extended support to Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders as party spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka claimed that multiple sources had warned that the three could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other equivalent provisions.“With you all the way 🪳🪳stay strong. ‘10 Oct poora desh aa raha hai…’,” O’Brien said in a post on X while replying to Dipke.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacting to the claim said they would not be intimidated by the possibility of action under laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) or National Security Act (NSA).“If the Govt believes that the threat of UAPA, NSA or years behind bars will scare us into silence, it won’t,” Dipke said in a post on X, adding that the protesters were prepared to spend “months or years in jail” but would not back down from their campaign to “save democracy”.He further said that they follow the path shown by Mahatma Gandhi and continue to resist “peacefully and non-violently”, despite what he described as attempts by the state to intimidate them.The developments come amid the CJP-led campaign against the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The protesters have been demanding accountability from chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the exercise and have announced further mobilisation on October 10 in Delhi.
Article Summary: AISA national president Neha Bora claims that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacting to the claim said they would not be intimidated by the possibility of action under laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act.

Article Title: ‘Racial attack’ by Delhi influencer on tribal youth roils Tripura
Article Text:
A controversial video featuring influencer Amir Shokeen allegedly mocking a tribal youth has ignited political backlash





AGARTALA/NEW DELHI: Political parties in Tripura closed ranks Wednesday over the alleged racial harassment in Delhi of a tribal youth from Gomati district and demanded legal action against social media influencer Amir Shokeen after a video purportedly showing him taunting the young man over his ethnicity circulated online.The clip, which surfaced Tuesday evening, purportedly shows Shokeen asking the youth if he is the "president" of a neighbouring country. He allegedly also mocks Tripura when the man responds he is Indian.CM Manik Saha of BJP directed the Tripura DGP to coordinate with Delhi Police and ensure a proper probe. CPM state secretary and lead-er of the opposition Jitendra Chaudhury demanded Shokeen apologise."Establish a precedent that is both resounding and unmistakable, ensuring no one ever dares insult Tripura and the Tiprasa community again," he said.Congress MLA Sudip Roy Barman called for a joint protest in Delhi. "This type of attitude is intolerable," he said.After TIPRA Motha chief Pradyot Kishore Debbarman called on the party's youth and students' wings to act, Youth Tipra Federation lodged a complaint accusing Shokeen of hate speech and defamatory remarks."Shokeen made crude and vulgar remarks..., calling him 'Chinese' and made fun of our state's name," said James Debbarma, general sec-retary of Youth Tipra Federation and an elected member of the Tripura tribal areas autonomous district council.Members of Twipra Students' Federation plan to meet the Delhi Police commissioner Thursday. "We are trying to identify the boy who was harassed and file a complaint," said general secretary Hamalu Jamatia.Shokeen has put out a video on Facebook claiming it was scripted. He said the target of his alleged abuse was an acquaintance who worked at a friend's cafe in Ahmedabad. "I did not intend to insult the people of Tripura, and I apologise if my words hurt anyone," he said.
Article Summary: Political parties in Tripura close ranks over the alleged racial harassment in Delhi of a tribal youth from Gomati district. A video purportedly showing Amir Shokeen taunting the young man over his ethnicity circulated online. The clip, which surfaced Tuesday evening, purportedly shows the youth asking the youth if he is the "president" of a neighbouring country.

Article Title: ‘Do you eat beef’: Coimbatore teacher under scanner after Dalit Class XI student dies by suicide
Article Text:
Peelamedu police have registered a case involving a teacher, headmaster, and two students related to a student’s suicide





COIMBATORE: Peelamedu police in the city have registered a case under three sections against four people, including two students of a government-aided school, in connection with the suicide of a Scheduled Caste student near Peelamedu.A. Akilan, 16, was a Class XI student of a government-aided school (KK Naidu) near Peelamedu. On Wednesday, his parents went to work while Akilan stayed at their home near Peelamedu.Upon returning from work, his mother, Kowsalya, found him hanging from the ceiling in a bedroom.She lodged a complaint with the Peelamedu police on Wednesday stating that Akilan had informed her that other students in the school were not talking to him after learning that he belonged to a Scheduled Caste.Furthermore, she alleged that the teacher had questioned the student about whether he ate beef, and the headmaster was accused of failing to take action regarding the incident.Peelamedu police have registered a case against the teacher, headmaster, and two fellow students in connection with Akilan's suicide, and further investigation is underway.
Article Summary: A. Akilan, 16, was a Class XI student of a government-aided school near Peelamedu. His mother, Kowsalya, found him hanging from the ceiling in a bedroom. Police have registered a case against the teacher, headmaster, and two fellow students.

Article Title: Crackdown on water wastage, illegal taps in Sambhajinagar
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Stepping up its campaign against water theft and wastage, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Municipal Corporation has begun imposing spot fines, disconnecting illegal tap connections and warning of criminal action against violators.A special squad on Wednesday fined three consumers a total of Rs 25,000 after finding drinking water being wasted at a hotel on Railway Station Road and a commercial complex in Osmanpura.“Every citizen is entitled to their rightful share of water. Water wastage and illegal connections will not be tolerated. Those using unauthorised connections should regularise them immediately or face penal and police action,” Yedge said.To intensify enforcement, the civic body also conducted a special training programme for its staff under the guidance of municipal commissioner G Sreekanth Yedge and additional commissioner Kalpita Pimple.Wednesday’s action follows an earlier inspection in Asefia Colony, where officials found treated water flowing onto the road. Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Municipal Corporation (CSMC) disconnected 39 unauthorised tap connections and imposed Rs 5,000 fine.
Article Summary: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Municipal Corporation has begun imposing spot fines, disconnecting illegal tap connections and warning of criminal action against violators. A special squad on Wednesday fined three consumers a total of Rs 25,000 after finding drinking water being wasted at a hotel and a commercial complex.

Article Title: Sangli DCC Bank poll: 19 elected unopposed
Article Text:
Kolhapur:





Setting aside their political rivalry, politicians of Mahayuti and MVA camps struck a rare deal for Sangli District Central Cooperative (DCC) Bank elections, resulting in 19 of the 21 seats being won unopposed on the final day for withdrawal of nominations.The unprecedented understanding between the two camps effectively turned the contest into a consensus election, leaving only two seats headed for polling on Nov 1. One seat is being contested by BJP MLA Gopichand Padalkar and the other by former MLA and NCP leader Ajitrao Ghorpade.As per the seat-sharing arrangement, seven are with NCP (SP) nominees, six with Congress, four with BJP, three with Shiv Sena and one is with NCP.The agreement comes despite strained political relations between the two alliances and was justified as a response to the severe drought prevailing in Sangli district.BJP functionary Prithviraj Deshmukh said chief minister Devendra Fadnavis had urged politicians to avoid a prolonged election battle and focus administrative and political attention on drought relief.“During a recent meeting at Kolhapur airport, chief minister Devendra Fadnavis urged Mahayuti politicians to avoid a divisive election battle amid the worsening drought.While Mahayuti was fully prepared for the contest, he said drought relief should take precedence and assured us he would speak to NCP (SP) functionary Jayant Patil and Congress neta Vishwajeet Kadam. After separate discussions, a consensus emerged, and Jayant Patil responded positively, paving the way for the maximum number of candidates to be elected unopposed,” Deshmukh said at a joint news conference of Mahayuti and MVA leaders.NCP (SP) politician Jayant Patil said the bank’s interests had been placed above party politics. “We have worked together before. This election is about the future of the bank, not political parties,” he said.The outcome also underlined the continuing dominance of influential political families in Sangli’s cooperative sector. Several candidates elected unopposed are either senior politicians themselves or close relatives of influential netas across party lines.Among them are sitting MLA Vishwajeet Kadam; Amol Babar, brother of Shiv Sena MLA Suhas Babar; Mahendra Lad, a relative of Kadam; Devraj Patil, a relative of Jayant Patil; Viraj Naik, son of outgoing chairman and former MLA Mansingrao Naik; former MLA Sumantai Patil, mother of NCP (SP) MLA Rohit R.R. Patil; Puja Patil, wife of Sangli MP Vishal Patil; and Varsha Sawant, wife of former MLA Vikram Sawant.
Article Summary: Politicians of Mahayuti and MVA camps struck a rare deal for Sangli District Central Cooperative (DCC) Bank elections. 19 of the 21 seats were won unopposed on the final day for withdrawal of nominations. The unprecedented understanding between the two camps effectively turned the contest into a consensus election.

Article Title: CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka seek more time, skip Delhi Police questioning
Article Text:
Delhi Police Crime Branch has summoned CJP leaders Sourav Das and Ashutosh Ranka to its Rajouri Garden office

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka will not appear before the Delhi Police Crime Branch for questioning on Thursday after seeking more time, sources told ANI. Police are expected to issue a fresh notice to the two leaders, the sources said.The Crime Branch had summoned Das and Ranka to its Rajouri Garden office on Thursday, a day after they were released from judicial custody.The two were released after a Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) court accepted their personal and surety bonds and recorded their written undertakings to maintain peace and abide by the law.SEM Ritu Raj directed them to furnish personal and surety bonds of Rs 50,000 each until the conclusion of the enquiry. They were also instructed to appear on every hearing date and comply with the conditions specified in their bonds and undertakings.In their written undertakings, the leaders promised not to breach peace or disturb public tranquillity. They also agreed not to call for protests at Jantar Mantar until the site is denotified in accordance with the law, and said any future demonstrations would be held within the constitutional framework.The two leaders were detained in connection with an October 13 protest at Jantar Mantar, which had been denotified as a designated protest site. Police alleged that they entered the area through private premises and violated conditions related to maintaining peace.The Delhi Police had earlier sought a further three-day extension of their judicial custody, citing concerns over a possible breach of peace and law and order. Police also pointed to alleged differences between statements made by the leaders before the court and their subsequent remarks to the media.The matter is scheduled for further proceedings before the SEM court on October 23 at 3 pm. Das, Ranka and their sureties have been directed to remain present.
Article Summary: Delhi Police Crime Branch has summoned CJP leaders Sourav Das and Ashutosh Ranka to its Rajouri Garden office. Police are expected to issue a fresh notice to the two leaders, the sources said. The two were released after a Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) court accepted their personal and surety bonds.

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Title: Man in Mahindra Thar with duplicate plate molests woman, knocks down another in Kharghar
Article Text:
30-year-old man was apprehended for allegedly molesting a woman and injuring another in Navi Mumbai.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team within 10 hours on Thursday evening.He had allegedly molested a 26-year-old woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night and, an hour later, severely injured a 22-year-old woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, Kharghar.Acting on a complaint by the woman allegedly molested by the Thar SUV driver, Kharghar police registered an FIR under BNS section 74 for the offence of assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.While, as per the complaint by the injured woman Shrawani Dandekar, a resident of sector 3, Belpada, an FIR under relevant BNS sections and Motor Vehicle Act was registered against the Thar SUV driver for rash and negligent driving causing hurt.The detained aaccused identified as Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of sector 50, Seawoods, Nerul was handed over to Kharghar police for further legal action.Previously, in January 2021, he was arrested by Nerul police in the FIR registered against him for alleged kidnapping, sexual harassment and molestation of a woman.Sanjay Joshi, senior inspector of Kharghar said, "The accused Nakhvi has been detained and subsequently it will be decided whether to arrest him or serve with a notice under Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for cooperating in police investigating."Audumbar Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-3 said, "After an FIR for molestation was registered at Kharghar police station by the victim woman, a resident of sector 34, Kharghar. As per the orders of higher authority, our team started a parallel probe. From the CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we obtained the red Thar SUV's registration number, which was of Vashi RTO passing.""When verified, the registration number was found to be that of a Maruti WagonR car. As the accused had used a duplicate registration number plate, we scrutinized as many as 62 Thar SUVs registered with various Regional Transport Offices (RTOs). Subsequently, we obtained the registration number of a red Thar SUV that was registered with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar RTO," Patil added.SPI Patil further informed, "The SUV was registered in the name of Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of Devaki Apartment in sector-50, Seawoods. From his mobile number registered with the RTO, his location was tracked.""He was apprehended from Bonkode village, Koparkhairane on Thursday late evening. Upon thorough interrogation, he confessed that he had inappropriately touched the woman pedestrian near Pethpada metro station while he drove his Thar SUV and sped away. He even confessed to have injured a woman pedestrian by hitting her his SUV while driving in Belpada area," he said.
Article Summary: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team on Thursday evening. He had allegedly molested a woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night. An hour later, he severely injured a woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, KharGHar.

Article Title: 2 women escape from RPF lockup in Navi Mumbai; 1 held after 6 hours, cop suspended
Article Text:
The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. (AI image)





NAVI MUMBAI: In a major security lapse at Belapur Railway Protection Force (RPF), two women arrested for allegedly attempting to steal overhead electric wires from the Juinagar railway godown escaped from the lockup after midnight on September 28.One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large.The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated against her.As per the FIR registered by RPF sub-inspector Milap Parte (52) at Panvel GRP, a case was registered on September 24 under Section 3(a) of the Railway Property (Unauthorized Possession) Act, 1966, Amendment 2012, at Belapur railway police station.The case was based on a written memo submitted by RPF personnel Ravikant Gade regarding the theft of overhead electric wires from the godown at Juinagar railway station on September 21.During the probe, a trap was laid on September 26 and around 1pm, two women were found loitering suspiciously near the Juinagar godown with the alleged intention of committing theft.They were taken into custody and identified as Rupali Kailas Kurhade (30), from Jalna, and Shalibai Ashok Pawar (49), from Bhiwandi.They were arrested after an FIR was registered for attempted theft and produced before a CSMT court, which remanded them to police custody till September 30. They were lodged in the lockup at Belapur RPF police station.Day-shift woman constable Rakhi Malaiya was assigned guard duty at the lockup, after which woman head constable Pooja Bagre was on night duty.Around 2am on September 28, when Bagre had gone to the toilet, the two women allegedly managed to open the lock by inserting their hands through the iron bars of the lockup and jerking it. Police suspect the lock may not have been secured properly.The women then reached the balcony at the rear end of the police station. They removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping.The incident was captured on CCTV footage. PSI Parte learnt about the escape after waking up at home around 6.30am and finding several missed calls from head constable Bagre and ASI Rajiv Parsan.Sunil Nila, chief spokesperson of Central Railway, said, "One accused woman Rupali Kurhade was apprehended from near Nerul railway station around 8.45 am. The other accused Shalibai Pawar is still absconding."
Article Summary: The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large. The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated.

Article Title: Ulhasnagar social activist Haresh Gajwani shot dead outside railway station, 3 arrested
Article Text:
Haresh Gajwani was murdered outside Ulhasnagar railway station on Wednesday night.





ULHASNAGAR: Police have arrested three suspects in connection with the murder of social worker Haresh Gajwani, who was shot dead outside Ulhasnagar railway station on Wednesday night. The suspects have been identified as Avinash Naidu, Vijay Singh and Noor Alam Khan.According to preliminary investigations, Gajwani and Naidu had a long-standing dispute. In 2021, counter-cases were registered against the two sides following a dispute, which allegedly contributed to continuing tensions between Gajwani and the accused.Police said the three suspects were traced and detained with the help of CCTV footage. Investigators are examining the alleged past rivalry, along with other possible motives behind the murder.Gajwani, 54, was allegedly attacked by three assailants who fired two rounds at him before fleeing the scene. Locals and police took him to Central Hospital, where doctors declared him "brought dead".Recently, Gajwani had posted on X, tagging senior officials from various police departments, as well as the chief minister, deputy chief minister and FDA commissioner Tukaram Mundhe. In his posts, he had highlighted alleged illegal activities in the area and claimed that some police personnel were supporting those involved. He had also expressed fears for his life, warning that the police personnel he had accused would also be responsible if anything happened to him.
Article Summary: Haresh Gajwani, 54, was shot dead outside Ulhasnagar railway station on Wednesday. Police have arrested three suspects in connection with the murder. The suspects have been identified as Avinash Naidu, Vijay Singh and Noor Alam Khan. Investigators are examining the alleged past rivalry, along with other possible motives.

Article Title: ‘Taken for granted since Ajit Pawar’s death’: NCP’s Makarand Patil airs workers’ anger against BJP over ‘unfriendly treatment’
Article Text:
Makarand Patil acknowledged the resentment among rank and file of party workers regarding their treatment by BJP

Pune





: Internal rifts within ruling Mahayuti alliance have burst into the open with senior NCP leader and state cabinet minister Makarand Patil claiming his party is being “taken for granted” following the demise of former deputy chief minister Ajit Pawar Patil made the remarks in Satara on Tuesday while addressing a party workers’ meeting convened to rally support for BJP candidates Kaustubh Gawade and Smita Jadhav, who are contesting the Pune division graduates’ and teachers’ constituencies. Several NCP workers from Satara district boycotted the meeting, highlighting the differences within Mahayuti.During his speech, Patil acknowledged the resentment among the rank and file regarding their treatment by BJP.“Some party workers have expressed their disappointment, and it is a fact that after Ajit Pawar’s death, our party is being taken for granted,” Patil said. “The complaints of our supporters are genuine. There has been lingering anger since the zilla parishad polls. Even in the recent MLC elections, a seat that rightfully belonged to us was given to our alliance partner. I spoke my heart out and raised this issue during the party’s core committee meeting.Despite his sharp critique, Patil urged workers to fall in line due to directives from top leadership. “Since our seniors have taken a call, and Sunetra vahini personally asked me to campaign for the Mahayuti candidates, I request all party workers to extend their support to them,” the minister added.Similar bickering has intensified between BJP and Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena over the Pune teachers’ constituency, where Shiv Sena is backing rebel candidate Sachin Sanap against BJP’s official nominee, Kaustubh Gawade.The dispute has triggered a war of words between cabinet colleagues. Speaking to the media in Solapur, senior BJP minister Jaykumar Gore dismissed the challenger, stating that “nobody knows Sanap.”Responding sharply, Shiv Sena minister Uday Samant countered, “Once the results are out for the MLC polls, everyone will know who Sanap is.”
Article Summary: Internal rifts within ruling Mahayuti alliance have burst into the open. Makarand Patil claims his party is being ‘taken for granted’ following the demise of former deputy chief minister Ajit Pawar Patil. Patil made the remarks while addressing a party workers’ meeting convened to rally support for BJP candidates.

Article Title: Court Grants 72-Hour Transit Remand Of Shraddha Dube To Lucknow Police
Article Text:
Accused Shraddha Dubey, driver Danish and Rashmi Dubey





Nagpur: After spending the night at Hudkeshwar police station, the trio of Shraddha Dubey, her sister Rashmi and driver Tanveer Ali were produced on Wednesday before the chief judicial magistrate S D Kamat, who granted 72-hour transit remand to Uttar Pradesh police.Before granting remand, the judge asked Dubey sisters and the driver if they had any complaints against the police, to which they replied in the negative. The court then directed UP cops to produce the accused before the chief judicial magistrate, Lucknow, by 2.50pm on October 24.The court also asked Shraddha whether she informed anyone about her arrest to which she confirmed that her lawyer was in the loop.Nagpur police exercised caution while handling Shraddha, a model, fashion blogger and social media influencer, given her ability to use digital platforms to communicate. She had earlier addressed the media through social media posts, claiming she had been implicated in the murder of Lucknow cafe owner Shiva Sharma . Custody protocols and legal formalities were followed, with her movements and police procedures documented.Assistant public prosecutor Shailendra Singh represented the prosecution, while Inspector Shreeprakash Singh from Hazratganj police station in Lucknow, accompanied the UP team.
Article Summary: Shraddha Dubey, her sister Rashmi and driver Tanveer Ali were produced on Wednesday before the chief judicial magistrate S D Kamat. The judge granted 72-hour transit remand to Uttar Pradesh police. The court then directed UP cops to produce the accused before the Chief judicial magistrate, Lucknow, by 2.50pm on October 24.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.

Article Title: Temple archakar, man arrested for temple hundi theft cases in Tiruchendur
Article Text:
Tuticorin

:





Two men were accused in separate hundi theft cases at the Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy Temple in Tiruchendur. While one accused, an archakar, was released on station bail, the other remanded in judicial custody despite both facing similar charges.According to police, the first case was registered at Tiruchendur Temple police station on October 16 under Section 305(c) (punishes theft committed in specific high-risk or sensitive locations) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) based on a complaint lodged by a temple official.The complaint alleged that Rs10,000 was stolen from a hundi located inside the temple premises between October 2 and 8.Police identified the accused as Muthan, 74, an archakar residing on South Car Street in Tiruchendur. During investigation, he was arrested at the police station. However, considering his advanced age and ill health, police released him on station bail.In a separate case, police registered a case on October 16 and arrested Murugan , 58, of Ariankuppam in Puducherry , for his involvement in a similar hundi theft of Rs10,000. He was remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: Two men were accused in separate hundi theft cases at the Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy Temple in Tiruchendur. While one accused, an archakar, was released on station bail, the other remanded in judicial custody.

Article Title: Arms exhibition to mark Police Martyrs Memorial Day
Article Text:
Madurai

:





ClearedMadurai district police organised an arms exhibition on Tuesday as part of the observance of Police Martyrs Memorial Day.According to police, the exhibition aims to create awareness about the weapons and equipment used by the police force and highlight the services and sacrifices of police personnel in safeguarding society.The exhibition was held at the Armed Reserve Office in Madurai from 10am to 6pm and was attended by school students and the general public.Deputy Inspector General of Police, Madurai Range, Abhinav Kumar , inaugurated the exhibition.
Article Summary: Madurai district police organised an arms exhibition on Tuesday as part of the observance of Police Martyrs Memorial Day. The exhibition was held at the Armed Reserve Office in Madurai from 10am to 6pm and was attended by school students and the general public.

Article Title: Traffic affected on Salem-Madurai National Highway after trailer truck crashes near Rasipuram
Article Text: NAMAKKAL: Traffic was affected for more than an hour on the Salem-Madurai National Highway near Rasipuram in Namakkal district on Thursday afternoon after a trailer truck crashed while descending the Andagalur Gate flyover.No casualties or injuries were reported.The truck was carrying about 60 tonnes of steel angles from Maharashtra to Karur. An officer at the Rasipuram police station said the driver lost control of the vehicle while descending the flyover around 1.30pm. The truck hit a streetlight pole on the roadside. “The vehicle partially blocked the road, causing congestion and delays for motorists and commuters,” he said.Vehicles piled up for two kilometres on the NH. The Rasipuram police reached the spot after receiving information, regulated traffic and moved the truck to the roadside.Police registered a case and were investigating the circumstances leading to the crash.
Article Summary: Trailer truck crashes on Salem-Madurai National Highway near Rasipuram. Truck was carrying 60 tonnes of steel angles from Maharashtra to Karur. Driver lost control of the vehicle while descending the flyover. No casualties or injuries were reported.

Article Title: Three arrested for attacking police officers in Elamkunnapuzha
Article Text:
Kochi

:





Three people were arrested for allegedly attacking police officers at a petrol pump in Elamkunnapuzha on Tuesday night.The incident occurred around 8.30pm after Njarakkal police received information about a fight at the petrol pump. Sub-inspector Jithin V and civil police officer Ragesh, who reached the spot to intervene, were allegedly stabbed and beaten with sticks. Both officers sustained serious injuries.The arrested persons are Prajith, 35, alias Munna, his brother Prajeesh, 36, both of Valakadavu in Njarakkal, and Ragin, 32, of Kadamakkudy.According to the police, Prajith and Ragin are listed as rowdy history sheeters. Prajith is an accused in 22 cases registered at Njarakkal, Munambam, Mattancherry and Viyyur police stations. Ragin is involved in seven cases registered at Varapuzha, Cheranalloor and Njarakkal. Prajeesh also faces another criminal case.The accused have been booked under various charges, including attempt to murder.The investigation is being conducted under the supervision of Ernakulam district police chief K S Sudarshan, with Munambam deputy superintendent of police S Jayakrishnan and inspector K K Shebab leading the probe.

: Former Rajasthan chief minister Ashok Gehlot and Rajasthan Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra on Thursday condemned the removal of photographs from Raihan Vadra’s exhibition at Bikaner House in Delhi, accusing the BJP govt of curbing freedom of expression.In a post on X, Gehlot wrote, “More than 70 photographs were removed from Raihan Vadra’s photo exhibition at Bikaner House in Delhi. Bikaner House is the property of the Rajasthan government. This means that, under the watch of the BJP government, the artistic expression of a young artist was stifled, which is highly condemnable.“Several photographs in the exhibition depicted youth movements in Delhi. The truth that comes before the public is what frightens the BJP the most. A government that is rattled by a photo exhibition wants to conceal the unjustified actions taken during these movements.“Raihan Vadra was asked to remove two photographs featuring the Tricolour, but he categorically refused to do so. His resolve is commendable. He has demonstrated that there can be no compromise when it comes to respecting the Tricolour.“Suppressing the voices of artists is a direct attack on democracy.This is a clear example of censorship. The BJP government must answer why photographs depicting the truth were removed.”Dotasra also criticised the removal of the artworks, alleging that the BJP sought to silence dissent whenever it became inconvenient.In a post on X, Dotasra wrote, “Whenever dissent becomes inconvenient, the BJP’s answer is to silence it.“74 artworks from Raihan Vadra’s exhibition at Delhi’s Bikaner House were removed. Artworks depicting peaceful protests were taken down for being “too political.”“Bikaner House is the property of the Rajasthan government, and this authoritarian decision was taken under the BJP government’s direction. Silencing art will not silence dissent.“This is the state of freedom of expression under the Modi government. But how long will this suppression continue?“I congratulate Raihan Vadra on his solo exhibition. His work will continue to challenge those in power and speak truth to power.”
